points.description: States that a binary search tree is a binary tree, i.e. a tree in which each node has at most two children.
States that the tree has an ordering/search property on its keys, not merely a binary structure.
States that for any/every node, the left child (or all keys in the left subtree) is smaller than the parent/node.
States that for any/every node, the parent/node is smaller than the right child (or all keys in the right subtree are larger than the node).
States that the ordering condition applies at every node throughout the tree, not only at the root.

rubric.notes: Full marks require saying it is a binary tree and giving the ordering property at every node: left smaller than parent and parent smaller than right. Part marks are earned for a partial definition, such as giving only one side of the ordering or applying it only to the root. No marks are earned for a reversed ordering or for a definition that only says it is a tree with two children.
